105	14. Mission priority
106	15. Optimize for larger orgs with lots of staff
107	#### Operations
108	16. CI / CD
109	17. Scalability, Observability, IaC, offline jobs, etc. 
110	
111	## Ambiguity resolution
112	1. Different skill taxonomy per org -> Skills owned by each org with fixed proficiency scale (1-5)
113	2. Different approval processes per org -> Initial scope will be one single director approval in code. Later extension to DB stored approval configs
114	3. Leads cannot approve their own missions -> One role per user with hierarchy Director > Lead, so a director can also lead missions. The mission lead can never approve their own mission. A director who is also leading a mission needs a second director to get approval. On mission creation the API and CLI flag that this mission requires an additional director for approval.
115	4. Who can be assinged to a mission: Only crew members can be assigned to missions. A lead is never a crew member and a director is never a crew member. The Director > Lead hierarchy does not include Crew.
116	5. Directors approve missions -> A mission to approve consists of requirements, timeline and date. Lead can preview the matcher in draft to check the mission can be staffed before submit. The director sees the same matcher preview in the approval view. Invites happen only after approval, so scarce skills are not reserved for unfunded missions. No separate steps for now
117	6. Changing after approval -> Missions can only be edited in draft. Before changing mission details after a director approved lead needs to withdraw the mission back to draft status. All INVITED / ACCEPTED assignments are then CANCELLED. Staffing changes (e.g. replacing a declined crew member) are not a change and need no new approval.
118	7. Availability tracking -> Instead of managing available periods it is more pragmatic to manage unavailable timeslots: holiday leave, sick leave, internal meetings, etc. Dates only. A crew member is blocked by unavailability, invited and accepted assignments.
119	8. Account for workload in matching -> Initially setting to booked mission days (invited + accepted) in time window (e.g. 90d) before and after the mission. Rest between missions deferred to P2
120	9. Crew has "limited" visibility -> Fixing to profile, own mission assignments and mission details. Enforced via RBAC in the API
121	10. Data must never leak across tenants -> Reads are protected by the org scoped data-access layer only. Composite foreign keys in DB protect writes / links. Error rule:
122	    - Resource does not exist -> 404
123	    - Resource exists in another org -> 404, so the response never reveals that it exists
124	    - Resource exists in the own org but the role has no access -> 403 with role and rule
125	11. Crews accept missions -> Crew members need to respond to approved missions. Only an approved mission is sent to the Crew members to ensure the whole mission is funded before reserving scarce skills for a mission. Otherwise skills might be missing for other missions currently being planned. 
126	12. Mission requirements -> A mission has slots: skill + minimum level. One skill per slot. One crew member fills max one slot per mission.
127	
128	## RBAC role resolution
129	- Directors 
130	    - Can do everything a lead can, on their own missions only
131	    - Cannot act on missions of other leads, except approve / reject
132	    - Can approve / reject missions (not their own)
133	    - Can view whole org data
134	    - Can edit org settings (skills)
135	- Leads
136	    - Can manage own missions (edit in draft only)
137	    - Can run matching on own missions and preview in draft and invite crew (approved only)
138	    - Can view all missions and crew of the org leave only shown as "unavailable", no reason
139	    - Cannot approve own missions
140	- Crew members
141	    - can view their own missions only
142	    - Can view mission details of their own missions
143	    - Can accept / decline mission assignments
144	    - Can view own assignment history
145	    - Can view and edit own profile: skills and unavailability
146	
147	## Tenant isolation
148	- Each user is assigned to one single organization for now
149	- JWT only carries user_id. Org and role are loaded from DB on each request -> role changes and revocation apply immediately. The cost is one primary key lookup per request. Decided.
150	- Every query needs to pass a data-access layer that checks their own org and the org data they want to retrieve / change
151	    - Every referenced id (e.g. skill_id, crew_id) is looked up with org filter. Cross org returns no data
152	- Composite foreign keys as second layer for writes so DB rejects cross org links even if the data-access layer has a bug. They do not protect reads. Reads rely on the data-access layer only
153	    - Every tenant table has org_id, parent tables have UNIQUE(org_id, id)
154	    - Child tables reference (org_id, x_id) -> parent(org_id, id): assignment -> mission / user, assignment (org_id, mission_id, requirement_id) -> mission_requirement (org_id, mission_id, id) so the slot belongs to the same mission, mission_requirement -> mission / skill, crew_skill -> user / skill, unavailability -> user, mission.lead_id -> user
155	    - Only crew can be assigned is not covered by FK -> checked in service layer
156	- Will ensure via cross org access checks in the happy path tests
157	- Postgres RLS would be the second layer for reads - Deferred to P2
158	
159	## Short references
160	UUID primary keys stay internal. Each resource also has a human readable key for the CLI, enforced by a DB unique constraint.
161	- Users: `username`, globally unique, because `mc login --user` has no org context. Crew references in the CLI use the username
162	- Skills: `slug` with UNIQUE(org_id, slug). A duplicate slug is rejected with a clear error, no auto suffix
163	- Missions: per org code `MSN-<n>` with UNIQUE(org_id, number). Next number via `UPDATE org SET mission_seq = mission_seq + 1 ... RETURNING` in the same transaction. The row lock serializes concurrent creates, so no collisions
164	- Slots: position in the mission (1, 2, 3) with UNIQUE(mission_id, position)
165	- Assignments: referenced by mission code. Partial unique index: one INVITED / ACCEPTED assignment per (mission_id, user_id)
166	- Slots: partial unique index on assignment (requirement_id) WHERE status IN (INVITED, ACCEPTED): one active assignment per slot
167	
168	## Initial mission lifecycle
169	1. DRAFT: Mission lead creates, edits mission. Can preview the matcher. If the lead is a director, the mission is flagged as requiring an additional director for approval. The flag is derived from the lead's current role and never stored
170	2. APPROVAL_REQUIRED:  Mission details are finalized. Mission is sent to Director for approval. Director sees the matcher preview. Awaiting response
171	    - Director rejects -> back to DRAFT (no comment, P2)
172	    - Lead withdraws -> back to DRAFT
173	3. APPROVED: Mission is approved and mission lead performs staffing. Inviting the crew. Awaiting their response. 
174	    - Lead withdraws mission back to DRAFT to change details -> all INVITED / ACCEPTED assignments become CANCELLED
175	4. ACTIVE: Mission lead started the mission. Guard: every slot has an ACCEPTED assignment
176	5. COMPLETED: Mission lead completed the mission
177	6. CANCELLED: Cancelled by mission lead (no reason, P2). Changing to this state from any state except COMPLETED. All INVITED / ACCEPTED assignments become CANCELLED.
178	- Transitions stored in code for now to reduce scope (from, to) -> allowed roles. Extension point for approval workflow customization later
179	
180	## Assignment lifecycle
181	1. INVITED: Lead invites crew member. Only when mission is APPROVED
182	2. ACCEPTED: Crew member accepted
183	3. DECLINED: Crew member declined. Slot is open again, lead reruns matching. The matcher never suggests this member for this mission again
184	4. CANCELLED: Mission went back to DRAFT or was cancelled. Frees the crew member's availability
185	- Double booking check when inviting and accepting: the service locks the crew member's user row (`SELECT ... FOR UPDATE`) and checks date overlap with INVITED / ACCEPTED assignments in the same transaction. No DB constraint, because mission dates are not on the assignment
186	
187	## Staffing matching v1
188	- Each slot seeks to be filled by one crew member (slot = skill + min level)
189	- P0: Include member in selection set if: 
190	    - Same org
191	    - Skill at minimum level
192	    - Available during timeframe / no unavailability during timeframe
193	        - other mission (invited or accepted)
194	        - leave
195	    - Has not declined this mission
196	- P0: Rematching only fills open slots (no INVITED / ACCEPTED assignment)
197	- P0: Rank / boost member in selection set if:
198	    - Lower workload than others
199	    - ~~(past mission with same skills? - member should update the proficiency themself then so exclude for now)~~
200	    - Be mindful of experts - could be required by other mission with higher proficiency requirement -> closest fit: proficiency closest to minimum ranks higher
201	    - Potential term: skill scarcity - fewer other members can fill slots with this skill -> member ranks lower to keep them free
202	- P0: All slots are matched together for now (linear optimization?)
203	    - Potential lib: scipy (`linear_sum_assignment`). Evaluate in the low level step
204	- Other constraints (resources, rest buffer, priority) left out for now, see P2
205	- P1: Rank breakdown: Why is this the best person for the slot
206	- P1: Decision insights for lead
207	    - Excluded members: Why?
208	    - P2: No matches: Report gap and potential resolutions: e.g. 2 qualified but on leave / other mission?
209	
210	
211	
212	## Proposed Tech stack
213	API + CLI. One language (Python) for API and CLI keeps the stack small
214	1. CLI Typer + httpx + Rich: typed commands, generated help, readable tables
215	    - CLI to API 
216	    - Stores the token locally after login
217	    - Table views by default, flag for scripting?
218	2. Backend FastAPI +Pydantic + SQLAlchemy with Alembic: Typed API with generated OpenAPI docs and safe DB access with migrations
219	    - Matching could require additional libs for optimization problem or naive solution? to be decided in low level step
220	    - Typed API client: shared Pydantic package in the same repository. API and CLI import the same request / response types. No generated OpenAPI client, so no regeneration step. The shared package depends on Pydantic only, no FastAPI or SQLAlchemy
221	3. Database: Postgres
222	4. Local JWT login with seeded users
223	    - Token only carries user_id, org and role loaded per request -> explained abovr
224	5. Orchestration of services / seeding of data via local docker-compose
225	
226	### MVP CLI commands v0
227	1. Login: mc login --user username, mc logout
228	2. Missions list: mc missions list
229	3. Mission detail: mc missions show MSN-42
230	    - Edit, submit, approve or reject: mc missions create|edit|submit|withdraw|approve|reject|cancel|start|complete
231	    - Staff with the matcher: mc missions match MSN-42, mc missions invite MSN-42 --slot 1 --crew username (APPROVED only)
232	4. My assignments (Crew): mc assignments list (current and history)
233	    - Accept, decline: mc assignments accept|decline MSN-42
234	5. My profile (Crew): mc profile show
235	    - Skills: mc profile skills set skill-slug --level n, mc profile skills remove skill-slug
236	    - Availability: mc profile availability list / add --from date --to date / remove id
237	
238	## Open questions / follow ups
239	- Additonal step required to indicate invited members? INVIATION_PENDING / STAFFING?
240	- Crew adds unavailability that overlaps an INVITED / ACCEPTED assignment: reject, warn or auto-decline?
241	- Crew lowers a skill level below a slot minimum while INVITED / ACCEPTED: keep, warn or flag to lead?
242	- API paths: short references (MSN-42) or UUIDs? Codes simplify the CLI, UUIDs keep paths stable if a code ever changes

A director who is also leading a mission needs a second director to get approval. On mission creation the API and CLI flag that this mission requires an additional director for approval.
4. Who can be assinged to a mission: Only crew members can be assigned to missions. A lead is never a crew member and a director is never a crew member. The Director > Lead hierarchy does not include Crew.
5. Directors approve missions -> A mission to approve consists of requirements, timeline and date. Lead can preview the matcher in draft to check the mission can be staffed before submit. The director sees the same matcher preview in the approval view. Invites happen only after approval, so scarce skills are not reserved for unfunded missions. No separate steps for now
6. Changing after approval -> Missions can only be edited in draft. Before changing mission details after a director approved lead needs to withdraw the mission back to draft status. All INVITED / ACCEPTED assignments are then CANCELLED. Staffing changes (e.g. replacing a declined crew member) are not a change and need no new approval.
7. Availability tracking -> Instead of managing available periods it is more pragmatic to manage unavailable timeslots: holiday leave, sick leave, internal meetings, etc. Dates only. A crew member is blocked by unavailability, invited and accepted assignments.
8. Account for workload in matching -> Initially setting to booked mission days (invited + accepted) in time window (e.g. 90d) before and after the mission. Rest between missions deferred to P2
9. Crew has "limited" visibility -> Fixing to profile, own mission assignments and mission details. Enforced via RBAC in the API
10. Data must never leak across tenants -> Reads are protected by the org scoped data-access layer only. Composite foreign keys in DB protect writes / links. Error rule:
    - Resource does not exist -> 404
    - Resource exists in another org -> 404, so the response never reveals that it exists
    - Resource exists in the own org but the role has no access -> 403 with role and rule
11. Crews accept missions -> Crew members need to respond to approved missions. Only an approved mission is sent to the Crew members to ensure the whole mission is funded before reserving scarce skills for a mission. Otherwise skills might be missing for other missions currently being planned. 
12. Mission requirements -> A mission has slots: skill + minimum level. One skill per slot. One crew member fills max one slot per mission.

## RBAC role resolution
- Directors 
    - Can do everything a lead can, on their own missions only
    - Cannot act on missions of other leads, except approve / reject
    - Can approve / reject missions (not their own)
    - Can view whole org data
    - Can edit org settings (skills)
- Leads
    - Can manage own missions (edit in draft only)
    - Can run matching on own missions and preview in draft and invite crew (approved only)
    - Can view all missions and crew of the org leave only shown as "unavailable", no reason
    - Cannot approve own missions
- Crew members
    - can view their own missions only
    - Can view mission details of their own missions
    - Can accept / decline mission assignments
    - Can view own assignment history
    - Can view and edit own profile: skills and unavailability

## Tenant isolation
- Each user is assigned to one single organization for now
- JWT only carries user_id. Org and role are loaded from DB on each request -> role changes and revocation apply immediately. The cost is one primary key lookup per request. Decided.
- Every query needs to pass a data-access layer that checks their own org and the org data they want to retrieve / change
    - Every referenced id (e.g. skill_id, crew_id) is looked up with org filter. Cross org returns no data
- Composite foreign keys as second layer for writes so DB rejects cross org links even if the data-access layer has a bug. They do not protect reads. Reads rely on the data-access layer only
    - Every tenant table has org_id, parent tables have UNIQUE(org_id, id)
    - Child tables reference (org_id, x_id) -> parent(org_id, id): assignment -> mission / user, assignment (org_id, mission_id, requirement_id) -> mission_requirement (org_id, mission_id, id) so the slot belongs to the same mission, mission_requirement -> mission / skill, crew_skill -> user / skill, unavailability -> user, mission.lead_id -> user
    - Only crew can be assigned is not covered by FK -> checked in service layer
- Will ensure via cross org access checks in the happy path tests
- Postgres RLS would be the second layer for reads - Deferred to P2

## Short references
UUID primary keys stay internal. Each resource also has a human readable key for the CLI, enforced by a DB unique constraint.
- Users: `username`, globally unique, because `mc login --user` has no org context. Crew references in the CLI use the username
- Skills: `slug` with UNIQUE(org_id, slug). A duplicate slug is rejected with a clear error, no auto suffix
- Missions: per org code `MSN-<n>` with UNIQUE(org_id, number). Next number via `UPDATE org SET mission_seq = mission_seq + 1 ... RETURNING` in the same transaction. The row lock serializes concurrent creates, so no collisions
- Slots: position in the mission (1, 2, 3) with UNIQUE(mission_id, position)
- Assignments: referenced by mission code. Partial unique index: one INVITED / ACCEPTED assignment per (mission_id, user_id)
- Slots: partial unique index on assignment (requirement_id) WHERE status IN (INVITED, ACCEPTED): one active assignment per slot

## Initial mission lifecycle
1. DRAFT: Mission lead creates, edits mission. Can preview the matcher. If the lead is a director, the mission is flagged as requiring an additional director for approval. The flag is derived from the lead's current role and never stored
2. APPROVAL_REQUIRED:  Mission details are finalized. Mission is sent to Director for approval. Director sees the matcher preview. Awaiting response
    - Director rejects -> back to DRAFT (no comment, P2)
    - Lead withdraws -> back to DRAFT
3. APPROVED: Mission is approved and mission lead performs staffing. Inviting the crew. Awaiting their response. 
    - Lead withdraws mission back to DRAFT to change details -> all INVITED / ACCEPTED assignments become CANCELLED
4. ACTIVE: Mission lead started the mission. Guard: every slot has an ACCEPTED assignment
5. COMPLETED: Mission lead completed the mission
6. CANCELLED: Cancelled by mission lead (no reason, P2). Changing to this state from any state except COMPLETED. All INVITED / ACCEPTED assignments become CANCELLED.
- Transitions stored in code for now to reduce scope (from, to) -> allowed roles. Extension point for approval workflow customization later

## Assignment lifecycle
1. INVITED: Lead invites crew member. Only when mission is APPROVED
2. ACCEPTED: Crew member accepted
3. DECLINED: Crew member declined. Slot is open again, lead reruns matching. The matcher never suggests this member for this mission again
4. CANCELLED: Mission went back to DRAFT or was cancelled. Frees the crew member's availability
- Double booking check when inviting and accepting: the service locks the crew member's user row (`SELECT ... FOR UPDATE`) and checks date overlap with INVITED / ACCEPTED assignments in the same transaction. No DB constraint, because mission dates are not on the assignment

## Staffing matching v1
- Each slot seeks to be filled by one crew member (slot = skill + min level)
- P0: Include member in selection set if: 
    - Same org
    - Skill at minimum level
    - Available during timeframe / no unavailability during timeframe
        - other mission (invited or accepted)
        - leave
    - Has not declined this mission
- P0: Rematching only fills open slots (no INVITED / ACCEPTED assignment)
- P0: Rank / boost member in selection set if:
    - Lower workload than others
    - ~~(past mission with same skills? - member should update the proficiency themself then so exclude for now)~~
    - Be mindful of experts - could be required by other mission with higher proficiency requirement -> closest fit: proficiency closest to minimum ranks higher
    - Potential term: skill scarcity - fewer other members can fill slots with this skill -> member ranks lower to keep them free
- P0: All slots are matched together for now (linear optimization?)
    - Potential lib: scipy (`linear_sum_assignment`). Evaluate in the low level step
- Other constraints (resources, rest buffer, priority) left out for now, see P2
- P1: Rank breakdown: Why is this the best person for the slot
- P1: Decision insights for lead
    - Excluded members: Why?
    - P2: No matches: Report gap and potential resolutions: e.g. 2 qualified but on leave / other mission?



## Proposed Tech stack
API + CLI. One language (Python) for API and CLI keeps the stack small
1. CLI Typer + httpx + Rich: typed commands, generated help, readable tables
    - CLI to API 
    - Stores the token locally after login
    - Table views by default, flag for scripting?
2. Backend FastAPI +Pydantic + SQLAlchemy with Alembic: Typed API with generated OpenAPI docs and safe DB access with migrations
    - Matching could require additional libs for optimization problem or naive solution? to be decided in low level step
    - Typed API client: shared Pydantic package in the same repository. API and CLI import the same request / response types. No generated OpenAPI client, so no regeneration step. The shared package depends on Pydantic only, no FastAPI or SQLAlchemy
3. Database: Postgres
4. Local JWT login with seeded users
    - Token only carries user_id, org and role loaded per request -> explained abovr
5. Orchestration of services / seeding of data via local docker-compose

### MVP CLI commands v0
1. Login: mc login --user username, mc logout
2. Missions list: mc missions list
3. Mission detail: mc missions show MSN-42
    - Edit, submit, approve or reject: mc missions create|edit|submit|withdraw|approve|reject|cancel|start|complete
    - Staff with the matcher: mc missions match MSN-42, mc missions invite MSN-42 --slot 1 --crew username (APPROVED only)
4. My assignments (Crew): mc assignments list (current and history)
    - Accept, decline: mc assignments accept|decline MSN-42
5. My profile (Crew): mc profile show
    - Skills: mc profile skills set skill-slug --level n, mc profile skills remove skill-slug
    - Availability: mc profile availability list / add --from date --to date / remove id

## Open questions / follow ups
- Additonal step required to indicate invited members? INVIATION_PENDING / STAFFING?
- Crew adds unavailability that overlaps an INVITED / ACCEPTED assignment: reject, warn or auto-decline?
- Crew lowers a skill level below a slot minimum while INVITED / ACCEPTED: keep, warn or flag to lead?
- API paths: short references (MSN-42) or UUIDs? Codes simplify the CLI, UUIDs keep paths stable if a code ever changes
